thesis: Coca-Cola's dominance stems from a franchise distribution model that pairs concentrate manufacturing with independent bottling partners, enabling global scale without owning all physical infrastructure while maintaining brand control and pricing power.

facts.claim: Coca-Cola beverages account for approximately 2.2 billion of an estimated 65 billion servings consumed worldwide daily, demonstrating unmatched global reach.
The concentrate operations model represented 85% of worldwide unit case volume in 2025 while generating 59% of company revenue, enabling asset-light growth.
Authorized bottling partners provide substantial local production, packaging, sales and distribution capabilities within the Coca-Cola system.
The Coca-Cola system's franchise model combines brand expertise and intellectual property with local operating infrastructure and customer relationships across territories.
The company's global franchise operating model combines the benefits of scale with deep, local market intimacy as a core strategic advantage.
The Coca-Cola system sold 33.8 billion unit cases in 2025, illustrating the scale advantage of the franchise distribution network.
